graph_diagnosis.summary: Pricing, vehicle deliveries, automotive revenue, and energy-segment performance form a reusable framework for assessing Tesla revenue momentum.
weaknesses: Margin compression is an indirect indicator of revenue growth.
The tax benefit affects earnings rather than revenue directly.

search_factors.why_search: Price reductions alter revenue per vehicle and can offset volume growth.
A lower average selling price translates delivery volume into less automotive revenue.
Delivery volume tests whether demand offsets pricing effects.
The automotive segment is the primary transmission channel to consolidated revenue.
Non-automotive segment growth can diversify consolidated revenue.
Separate earnings-only items from revenue drivers when interpreting results.

checkpoints.mechanism: Aggressive price cuts lower revenue per vehicle even when they support demand.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Track price changes and vehicle revenue per unit.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Higher mix or price increases lift revenue per vehicle.

checkpoints.mechanism: Record deliveries can partly offset lower revenue per vehicle.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Compare delivery growth with pricing and revenue per vehicle.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Delivery volume falls or does not convert into revenue.

checkpoints.mechanism: Average selling price and deliveries combine to determine automotive revenue growth.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Reconcile automotive revenue growth to volume and pricing.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Automotive revenue grows despite weak price realization.

checkpoints.mechanism: Energy growth can add revenue outside the automotive segment.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Check energy segment growth and its share of total revenue.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Energy growth slows or is too small to matter.

checkpoints.mechanism: Automotive price-volume realization and energy revenue combine into quarterly revenue-growth acceleration.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Calculate year-over-year growth and compare it with the prior quarter after reconciling segment contributions.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Segment trends do not reconcile to consolidated revenue.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Price cuts reduce average selling price, which can weaken automotive revenue momentum and consolidated revenue growth.
applicability_conditions: Pricing reductions are broad enough to affect quarterly realization.
failure_conditions: Volume or vehicle mix more than offsets lower prices.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Higher deliveries support revenue when volume gains convert into automotive sales.
applicability_conditions: Demand and production sustain delivery growth.
failure_conditions: Lower price realization offsets additional units.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Energy-segment growth can cushion automotive weakness in consolidated revenue.
applicability_conditions: Energy growth is material relative to automotive revenue.
failure_conditions: The segment is too small to offset automotive changes.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Delivery growth offsets lower average selling prices.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminating_evidence: Compare automotive revenue per delivered vehicle with delivery growth.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Energy growth becomes large enough to offset automotive weakness.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminating_evidence: Measure energy revenue contribution against automotive revenue changes.

forecast_audit_questions: Do price reductions lower revenue per vehicle?
Do delivery gains offset pricing pressure in automotive revenue?
How much does energy growth contribute to consolidated revenue?
Do segment results reconcile to the calculated acceleration?
